Chapter 9: The Enneagram in Relationships—Building Bridges, Not Walls.
If there’s anywhere Enneagram wisdom really shines, it’s in our relationships—whether you’re talking about marriage, friendship, or family. The patterns we each bring to the table can either help us build bridges to one another, or, without even realizing it, put up walls.
Now, the Enneagram isn’t some magic solution that’ll fix every conflict. But, it does give us a way to understand what’s really going on beneath the surface—what drives us, and what drives the people we care about.
Picture a couple who keep having the same old argument. One person always feels criticized, while the other feels totally ignored. They go around in circles, both convinced the other just doesn’t get it. But, once they start exploring their Enneagram types, something changes. Suddenly, they realize their reactions aren’t just about what’s happening right now—they’re shaped by old fears and hopes. Maybe the perfectionist in the relationship feels unloved when things aren’t just right, while the peacemaker feels completely overwhelmed by conflict.
With this kind of understanding, the argument becomes less about blaming each other, and more about showing compassion.
Friendships are shaped by these patterns, too. Some friends need a lot of reassurance, while others crave their independence. Some get a spark from new adventures, while others would rather stick to what they know. The Enneagram won’t erase these differences, but it helps us navigate them better. Suddenly, you can actually appreciate what each person brings to the friendship, and you know how to show up for them in ways that really matter.
I remember a group of friends who always seemed to talk past each other. One wanted deep, thoughtful conversations. Another kept things light. A third was always dreaming up the next adventure. For years, their differences just led to frustration. But when they started learning about the Enneagram, they began to see each other in a new light. The deep thinker wasn’t being difficult—they just needed meaning. The planner wasn’t flaky—they just needed variety.
That understanding helped the group connect in new ways, support each other better, and even celebrate what made each of them unique.
The Enneagram also comes in handy when it comes to conflict. Most of us try to avoid it, worried it’ll lead to rejection or pain. But the Enneagram reminds us that conflict is part of being human—and that it can actually help us get closer. When you get a handle on your own patterns, and start to recognize the patterns of the people you love, it gets a little easier to have those honest conversations, to apologize, and to forgive.
Relationships aren’t easy. They take patience, humility, and a real willingness to see things from someone else’s perspective. The Enneagram doesn’t make it effortless, but it does make it possible.
It reminds us that everyone’s doing the best they can, shaped by their own fears and hopes. And with that kind of understanding, relationships shift—they become less about fixing each other, and more about simply walking alongside each other, with patience and a little bit of grace.
